extracted.intended_audience: researchers and policymakers interested in health policy, rehabilitation services, and systematic review methods (esp. Portuguese context)
extracted.subtask_description: A systematic documentary review of official Portuguese government programmes and strategic health documents (1995–2025) assessing how physical rehabilitation is referenced, integrated, and operationalized, using PRISMA-adapted procedures, the SPIDER framework, and qualitative thematic analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of PRISMA guidelines (adapted)
rubrics_metrics.description: The review follows the PRISMA guidelines for systematic reviews, adapted to the analysis of policy and strategic documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply PRISMA steps (structured search, transparent screening/selection, flow reporting) but adapt terminology and procedures to documentary/policy sources rather than primary research studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: SPIDER analytical framework
rubrics_metrics.description: The analytical structure of the study is guided by the SPIDER framework, which is suitable for qualitative and documentary research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify SPIDER components for the review: Sample = official national policy documents; Phenomenon of Interest = presence and operationalization of rehabilitation-related measures; Design = qualitative documentary analysis; Evaluation = how rehabilitation policies/measures are described and structured.

rubrics_metrics.name: Systematic search of official repositories
rubrics_metrics.description: The research involves a systematic search of official Portuguese government repositories and institutional sources, including the Government Portal, the Electronic Official Gazette, and websites of national health authorities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cover multiple official sources to maximize completeness; document exact sources and search procedures for reproducibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Predefined inclusion/exclusion criteria and timeframe
rubrics_metrics.description: Documents are screened according to predefined inclusion and exclusion criteria to ensure that only official state documents published within the specified time frame are analyzed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define and report inclusion/exclusion rules explicitly (e.g., official state documents only, publication date range 1995–2025) and apply them consistently during screening.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specified document types (sample scope)
rubrics_metrics.description: The sample consists of official national policy documents, including Government Programs and strategic health documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearly list which types of government/strategic documents are eligible (e.g., Government Programmes, strategic health plans) and exclude non-official or subnational documents unless pre-specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standardized data extraction framework
rubrics_metrics.description: Relevant information is extracted from each document using a standardized data extraction framework that records characteristics such as publication year, document type, institutional source, and textual references related to rehabilitation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a predesigned extraction form and report the fields captured (at minimum: year, document type, issuing institution, verbatim or coded rehabilitation references); ensure extraction consistency (pilot, double extraction if feasible).

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualitative thematic analysis to identify framing
rubrics_metrics.description: Following data extraction, the documents undergo qualitative thematic analysis to identify how rehabilitation is framed within health policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conduct thematic coding of extracted text to generate themes about framing (e.g., priorities, target populations, service models); describe coding procedure and how themes were derived.

rubrics_metrics.name: Temporal and comparative perspective
rubrics_metrics.description: The analysis also incorporates a temporal and comparative perspective, examining how references to rehabilitation appear across different governmental cycles and policy contexts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare documents across time periods and political/governmental cycles to identify evolution, continuities, and discontinuities; explicitly report comparative methods and time slices used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document quality assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: The study includes an assessment of document quality based on factors such as institutional credibility, clarity, relevance to rehabilitation policy, and degree of operational detail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess and report document-level quality using the stated factors (institutional credibility, clarity, relevance, operational detail); define scoring or judgement rules for each factor and apply consistently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation of presence, integration, and operationalization
rubrics_metrics.description: The phenomenon of interest is the presence and operationalization of rehabilitation-related measures — the extent to which Portuguese Government Programs and national strategic health documents refer to, integrate, or operationalize measures related to physical rehabilitation (including Physical and Rehabilitation Medicine and Physiotherapy).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish between mere mention, integrated policy positioning, and concrete operational measures (e.g., targets, budgets, implementation mechanisms); code and report examples for each level.
